attributes.action: Grant greater powers to Councils with waterways to become the senior Custodians
attributes.additional_details:
Gloucester’s Historic Dock is dying. 
The Canal & River Trust has proven they cannot care for our waterways alone, due to financial pressures.
Giving some of its decision making powers within sections of its waterway to a democratically elected body, would give more accountability on how our waterways are managed. 
For Gloucester that would mean the Dock custodianship being in the hands of the people, not a struggling charitable trust & delivering a brighter future for its next 200 years.
attributes.background:
The Government to grant powers to Local Authorities for custodianship of waterways that are an integral part of their community. 
The Canal & River Trust are failing in the care of our waterways.
Granting powers to a democratic Council would give more accountability on how waterways are managed.

rejection.details: I'm afraid we find this petition unclear. Some local authorities already act as custodians /owners of local waterways (rivers, docks and canals). Are these new powers to enable local authorities to seize control of waterways from current custodians/owners, whether public bodies, charities or other private organisations?
